faqs.q: What is the NATO phonetic alphabet?

faqs.a: Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta, Echo, Foxtrot, Golf, Hotel, India, Juliett, Kilo, Lima, Mike, November, Oscar, Papa, Quebec, Romeo, Sierra, Tango, Uniform, Victor, Whiskey, X-ray, Yankee, Zulu.

faqs.a: Over radio static, 'nine' can sound like the German word 'nein' (no), and 'three' can be confused with 'free'. The special pronunciations Niner and Tree were chosen for maximum clarity.
faqs.q: Why is 9 pronounced Niner and 3 pronounced Tree?

keyFacts: The alphabet was finalized by NATO in 1956 after testing hundreds of words with speakers of 31 nationalities.
Every word was chosen to be instantly recognizable even over static and heavy accents: no two words sound alike.
Digits have special forms: 9 is pronounced Niner and 3 is Tree to avoid confusion over radio.
It is used worldwide by pilots, soldiers, emergency services, call centers and logistics teams.
The same spelling alphabet is also called the ICAO phonetic alphabet and the ITU alphabet.
